DA42 NG-6 Performance Calculator V3

AFM Performance — Doc. 7.01.16-E Rev. 5, 10-Jun-2021 • training aid

Take-off

Enter the actual take-off mass. Weight is interpolated only between published masses within the selected procedure; the normal and short-field procedures are kept separate because the AFM uses different flap settings and speeds.

Normal Landing

Normal landing performance uses the AFM Flaps LDG landing tables. Weight, pressure altitude and OAT are interpolated between the published values.

Landing - Abnormal Flap

Abnormal flap landing performance uses the AFM abnormal flap-position tables (APP or UP). Weight, pressure altitude and OAT are interpolated between the published values.

All-engine climb

Show climb gradient calculation

Uses the AFM gradient formula with TAS derived from the published Vy airspeed and the OAT already entered above.

AFM conditions: both engines 92%, gear retracted, vY. The AFM publishes 1700, 1900 and 1999 kg tables for both UP and APP; mass is interpolated between neighbouring published weights.

OEI climb

Show climb gradient calculation

Uses the AFM gradient formula with TAS derived from VYSE = 85 KIAS and the OAT already entered above.

AFM conditions: remaining engine 92%, dead engine feathered/secured, flaps UP, gear retracted, VYSE 85 KIAS, one ball out, max 5° bank.

Time / Fuel / Distance to climb

Enter the actual climb weight. The AFM publishes 1700, 1900 and 1999 kg tables; the calculator linearly interpolates between neighbouring published masses, then subtracts the cumulative starting-altitude values from the target-altitude values as shown in the AFM example.

Go-around climb

AFM: flaps LDG, both power levers MAX, gear extended. vREF 84 KIAS up to 1900 kg and 86 KIAS above 1900 kg. Mass is interpolated between published 1700, 1805, 1900 and 1999 kg tables.

Cruise performance

The AFM cruise tables are for 1999 kg, flaps UP, gear retracted. Enter actual OAT; the calculator derives ISA temperature and ISA deviation, then interpolates the published deviation columns and pressure-altitude rows. Cruise mass is fixed by the AFM table and is not weight-interpolated.

Stall speeds

AFM: most forward CG, power off. KIAS values may not be accurate at stall.

Interpolation method

What the AFM says

The AFM states: for temperatures, altitudes and weights between those provided, use linear interpolation between neighbouring values.

2-D table calculation

For a value between two pressure-altitude rows and two OAT columns:

fT = (OAT − OAT_low) / (OAT_high − OAT_low) L = LowRow_lowTemp + fT × (LowRow_highTemp − LowRow_lowTemp) U = HighRow_lowTemp + fT × (HighRow_highTemp − HighRow_lowTemp) fPA = (PA − PA_low) / (PA_high − PA_low) Result = L + fPA × (U − L)

Weight interpolation

fW = (W − W_low) / (W_high − W_low) Result = LowWeightResult + fW × (HighWeightResult − LowWeightResult)

Audit trail

Each calculator reports the lower/upper brackets, interpolation fractions and source values used. It does not extrapolate outside the digitised table range.

Important: this is a training aid. Verify all calculations against the current aircraft AFM and FTE/operator procedures before operational use.
